source.title: From Evasion to Concealment: Stealthy Knowledge Unlearning for LLMs
source.authors: Tian-Le Gu; Kexin Huang; Ruilin Luo; Yuanqi Yao; Xiuying Chen; Yu-Jiu Yang; Yan Teng; Ying-Chun Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure text is garbled or flattened, but the main text and relevant table values are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study discusses unlearning stealth and evaluates attacks that detect signs of unlearning, but it does not test whether the attacks named in the claim recover forgotten knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper's PPL and consistency attacks detect detectable output patterns; they do not recover forgotten facts. Its Min-K% evaluation is a membership-inference measure, not a knowledge-recovery attack. The ToFU forget-quality values measure similarity to a retain model, not targeted-knowledge accuracy or attack recovery, so they are not recorded as rows for these versions. The paper's cited jailbreak results are from other work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes MEOW, an unlearning method that fine-tunes on inverted facts, and evaluates it on ToFU. It reports forget quality (a p-value for similarity to the retain model), model utility, NLU/NLG scores, Min-K% membership inference, and two detectability heuristics. It never applies any recovery attack the versions name: relearning fine-tuning, direction ablation, quantization, or rephrasing, jailbreak or in-context prompting. It also does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy recovered under attack. So no version is tested. Robustness is claimed only against membership inference and detectability, so it does not count as a test of F.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that MEOW improves ToFU forget quality without retain data or auxiliary models, preserves utility and NLU/NLG ability, and is more resilient to Min-K% membership inference. They also argue that refusal and garbled outputs are detectable unlearning traces. Their statement that App. A shows these traces enable successful jailbreaks is not supported: App. A measures detectability of target responses only and runs no jailbreak.
record.recipe_differences: MEOW selects generated inverted facts using MEMO and fine-tunes with gradient descent. It is not the original unlearning recipe in the claim. The paper reports code and datasets as released, but gives only the linked name “MEOW-repo” in the provided text.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that MEOW's number of inverted facts and high-versus-low MEMO selection strategy require tuning and affect utility and forget quality; the direction of the forget-quality effect changes around four facts.

fits_no_version.finding: PPL and embedding-consistency heuristics flag garbled (ASR 99.5/98.5%) and refusal-template (consistency ASR 70.5%) target responses as signs of unlearning. Inverted-fact targets are flagged less often (PPL ASR 15%, consistency ASR 0%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hard-unlearning target styles (garbled text, template refusal) leave output signatures that reveal what was unlearned. Plausible false answers are less detectable.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Min-K% (K=5) membership inference on ToFU-5% forget answers, MEOW shows higher robustness than baselines with F.Q. ≥0.05. NPO+GD is similar.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning by fine-tuning on inverted facts reduces membership-inference signal on forgotten data relative to GA/NPO-style methods.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics, ACL 2025
record.problems: The supplied Figure 5 is not numerically readable, and the paper's robustness measure is membership inference rather than recovery of forgotten knowledge. Appendix A's attacks detect output-pattern signatures rather than testing the claimed recovery attacks.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted under the 60-row limit. ToFU forget-quality table values were not entered as rows because the metric is described as similarity to the retain model and does not measure recovery under the attacks in the claim.

untested.parts: There is no targeted-knowledge accuracy versus chance and no recovery attack. Forget quality is a distributional p-value, not accuracy.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack on unlearned models.
No activation ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery test. The jailbreak risk is asserted via a citation of Lynch et al., not measured.
MEOW is tested only against Min-K% membership inference and output-pattern detectability, not against the B–E attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses classification is kept. One correction: the App. A rows describe target-label datasets rather than unlearned model outputs. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance together with recovery attempts by the specified attacks.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion is tested.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context knowledge-recovery attack is tested.
MEOW is evaluated against membership inference and unlearning-trace detection, not the attacks named in versions B–E.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-7B-Chat
rows.operation_detail: PPL attack detects garbled or otherwise unusual outputs; threshold PPL > 200
rows.note: Measures detectability of an output pattern, not recovery of forgotten knowledge.
rows.check: Table 5 (App. A) scores constructed target-response datasets (garbled, refusal-template, inverted facts) concatenated with ToFU-5% questions. It does not score outputs of unlearned LLaMA2-7B-Chat models. Subject 'LLaMA2-7B-Chat' and the 'unlearning_method' condition overstate the setup. These are target-label detectability values, not model behaviour after unlearning.
